# Archive fixtures

ZIP/TAR/TGZ fixtures are generated by `scripts/generate-archive-fixtures.py`.
They deliberately include unsafe paths, links, duplicate files and special files.

RAR fixtures are decoded from the pinned libarchive 3.8.9 test suite:
`test_read_format_rar.rar.uu`, `test_read_format_rar_binary_data.rar.uu`,
`test_read_format_rar5_stored.rar.uu`, and `test_read_format_rar5_compressed.rar.uu`.
Source: https://www.libarchive.org/downloads/libarchive-3.8.9.tar.xz
SHA256: `888c934f9d95648ecb9163dc8e23ab80a476ecb81a8f1154704a227b5b676dde`.
The basic RAR contains a symlink and must be rejected. The binary-data RAR
and stored/compressed RAR5 fixtures must extract successfully. See LICENSE.txt.

## Generated 7z fixtures

All `.7z` files contain synthetic project-owned data, not third-party documents.
They are genuine 7z containers generated by `scripts/generate-7z-fixtures.py`
using official [7-Zip 26.04](https://github.com/ip7z/7zip/releases/tag/26.04).
Development generator archive: `7z2604-mac.tar.xz`, SHA256
`bee04358cbcbc7106273cee0e8d72916db2696c48067a3538c34d8cd6fd16578`.
7-Zip's distribution notices apply to that development tool; no tool binary or
third-party data is included here. Builds, tests and runtime need no 7-Zip CLI.
Regeneration checks the tool version, disables timestamps and uses one thread.
`7z-manifest.json` records archive hashes and expected decoded hashes/content.
The generator proves the small solid fixture has multiple files in one block.

| Fixtures | Purpose and expected result |
| --- | --- |
| safe-copy, safe-lzma, safe-lzma2 | Non-solid Copy/Store, LZMA, LZMA2; byte-perfect success |
| safe-solid-lzma2, unicode-names | Solid LZMA2; nested/empty directories, spaces, Cyrillic/Unicode, binary and empty files; success |
| safe-bcj-lzma2 | Native x86 BCJ + LZMA2 on synthetic branch bytes; success |
| large-solid-lzma2 | 384 MiB output in three nested 128 MiB files, 16 MiB dictionary; streamed success or cancellation with cleanup |
| encrypted, encrypted-header | Synthetic fixture password, data/header encryption; EARCHIVE_ENCRYPTED, no published output |
| corrupted, truncated | Damaged solid payload / truncated genuine container; EARCHIVE_FORMAT |
| unsupported-bzip2 | Valid 7z using disabled BZip2 codec; EARCHIVE_UNSUPPORTED_CODEC |
| huge-dictionary | Genuine LZMA2 container with property changed to UINT32_MAX and CRCs rebuilt; EARCHIVE_LIMIT before huge allocation |
| single-copy | Stored source for unsafe-name mutations; valid control container |
| duplicate | Stored container with two names changed to one, CRCs rebuilt; reject, no output |
| dotdot, absolute, drive, unc, ads, reserved, reserved-nul, trailing, backslash, control | Valid stored containers with unsafe UTF-16 names and rebuilt header CRCs; EARCHIVE_UNSAFE_PATH |
| unsafe-link | Genuine Unix symlink entry, created with `-snl`; EARCHIVE_UNSAFE_ENTRY |

All names in the table have the `.7z` suffix. Unsafe files intentionally remain
valid containers so rejection exercises entry/decoder policy rather than merely
an invalid signature. None may publish partially extracted output or overwrite
an existing destination. The password is synthetic test data, not a user secret.
Fixture filenames themselves must be portable to Windows: `reserved-nul.7z`
contains the unsafe `NUL.txt` entry without using a reserved device name for the
outer archive checked out by Git.
